conventions.si_mapping: '4.1': si := raw_intensity of kala_gochara_windows, exactly as stored (the unsigned magnitude) — SI addendum v1.4 §1a. NOT signed_intensity: the 4.x writer stores signed_intensity = raw_intensity x (-1 if is_adverse else 1), negative on every adverse window, which protocol §4.5 rejects. Like-for-like with '3.0': in generation '3.0' signed_intensity == raw_intensity on all 914 rows (none negative; 330 adverse rows positive), so the pinned '3.0' si is the same quantity. The extract command stops if any row has |signed_intensity| != raw_intensity or raw_intensity < 0. raw_intensity is NOT NULL, so no unknown competitor can occur in a '4.1' extract: the run asserts unknown_si_rows = 0 and discloses any other value. The governed-5.x mapping (si := evidence_for) is untouched.

thresholds.t_honesty: UNVERIFIABLE — DETERMINED (Stream A relay M20261002T042919-8f9e, from the writer code). Protocol §6.5 defines coverage per CLASS as (class, year) cells computed ÷ (class, year) cells in the horizon, from a manifest naming those cells. The '4.1' chain writes kala_gochara_coverage rows per BODY-TARGET partition (partition_kind='body_target', key '<body>:<target_type>'; 8 persisted bodies — Moon is on-demand, never persisted) — there are NO event_class partitions and NO year cells. A per-(class, year) coverage fraction therefore cannot be computed from them without a class->(body, target_type) mapping that no governed source declares, and none is invented here. Result: t_honesty.status = UNVERIFIABLE, pass false, and by protocol §6.5(b) the '4.1' candidate is NOT flip-eligible under v2.3 whatever its other endpoints show; the measurement still runs for T-cover/T-time/T-rank/T-FP as a diagnostic. A route to verifiability needs a NEW decision made before any result: either per-(class, year) coverage rows for '4.1' (the governed 5.x chain's event_class partitions) or a protocol amendment declaring a class<->partition mapping from a governed source. The '3.0' manifest is never substituted.

rerun_policy: The scorer is deterministic: a same-input rerun must reproduce the result file byte for byte (checked once, recorded). After any candidate result has been inspected NO frozen item may change; a change is a protocol violation and is disclosed as one (addendum §5). A discovered defect in the adapter/scorer is reported and fixed in a new, separately-dated freeze, never patched into this run.

ephemeris_requirement.kind: NAMED STAGE-1 REQUIREMENT — a precondition of the governed '4.1' RUN, verified at freeze by manifest read-back (steward M20261002T042929-e773). Until it is met the freeze cannot be FROZEN and no extract may be generated.
ephemeris_requirement.why: The '4.1' manifest input vector carries NO ephemeris or implementation identity (no opened-file hashes, no swisseph library hash; it predates AM-16). Production L1 was found to have run on the Moshier fallback; a measurement whose ephemeris cannot be identified afterwards is not acceptable.
ephemeris_requirement.requirement: Before the governed '4.1' run, the candidate writer's manifest records the ephemeris identity as ONE definition shared with '5.0' (AM-16 ephemeris component, schema ka_gochara_input_vector/2): key `ephemeris` = {backend:'swieph', swe_version, library_sha256 (sha256 of the loaded swisseph artifact), platform ('<system>-<machine>'), files {<.se1 name>: sha256} — the files the kernel actually OPENS for the consumed bodies over the consumed horizon, probe_digest (fixed series probe)}, and the writer REFUSES (raises, no manifest published) when the identity cannot be established or any probe is served by the Moshier fallback.
